name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention; domain animate, descriptor party_addition_with_appear_effect. Accurately reflects purpose (plays the 'new char appearance' 12-frame animation when a party member is added). No Ghidra address residue.
purpose: Plays the 12-frame 'new character appearance' animation (explosion/sparkle sprites + appearance-chime SFX) for newly joined party members, spawning them via the race-id-filtered portrait loader and compositing them into the battle field view.
logic_summary: Setup: loads the appearance chime (fd2_load_dat_resource FDOTHER.DAT,0,0x5F) and the explosion sprite-sheet (idx 9) from FDOTHER.DAT; malloc(0x25680) backup buffer and snapshots large_game_state_buffer into it; records old_char_count = party_member_count; then fd2_load_chapter_portraits_and_dump_tmp(target_race_id) spawns the field chars whose race byte matches the arg (growing party_member_count). Then a do/while over snapshot 0..0xB: at snapshot==1 play the chime; each frame restore the working surface from backup, read per-frame source offset src_off = explosion_sprite[snapshot*4+6], and for every newly-added char (index old_char_count..party_member_count) whose (pos_x,pos_y) lies inside the battle view window, blit the explosion sprite into the buffer at (pos_y-origin_y)*0x2AC0 + (pos_x-origin_x-1)*0x18 + 0x75D8; then fd2_blit_rectangle paints the frame to the mode13h primary at 0xA0504. Frames 6/7/8 are special composite beats: frame 6 restores backup, paints old chars then new chars (skip flags&1 dead) using the buffer-base pointer-shift trick (base -= 0xE40 around the new-char loop), runs fd2_paint_chars_shadow_overlay, saves back to backup; frame 7 is the same but composites the battle tile map first and shifts base by -0x8E8; frame 8 composites the tile map then fd2_composite_all_chars_overlay (which handles its own shadow) and saves back to backup. Every frame ends with fd2_clear_keyboard_buffer + fd2_wait_n_bios_ticks(1). On exit (snapshot>0xB) frees explosion_sprite, backup, sfx_buf and returns.

params.name: target_race_id
params.semantics: Joining recruit / party-slot id, forwarded directly to fd2_load_chapter_portraits_and_dump_tmp as the race-match filter selecting which field chars spawn into the party. Call sites pass small slot ids (1, 2, 4, 5). NOT a chapter id; the chapter index is read separately from data_fd2_chapter_current_chapter_id inside the loader.
params.reason: Name accurately captures its role as the race-id match filter; no address residue, not a generic param_N.

comment_original_issue: Comment body referenced the obsolete Ghidra-native name param_1 in three spots (overview sentence and the two fd2_load_chapter_portraits_and_dump_tmp setup bullets) while the actual source parameter is named target_race_id; the bottom Args section already used target_race_id, so the block was internally inconsistent.
notes: Source implementation matches the decompilation exactly (logic verified, not re-validated). The data_fd2_large_game_state_buffer_ptr 'write' is the documented temporary pointer-shift trick (base -= 0xE40 / -= 0x8E8 then restored within the same frame) so the shared paint helper fd2_paint_char_sprite_at_world_pos writes to a shifted base; it is restored before the frame ends, so it is not a net mutation of game state. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with the refined understanding (it uses the Ghidra-native param_1 name, appropriate for a plate), so it was left unchanged.
